cues.text: Let us bring together the main ideas from this session.
We began with digital transformation, which changes how organisations create value.
Alongside it, disruptive technologies enable new capabilities that were not possible before.
Next, we looked at the financial tools used to judge investments.
Total cost of ownership, or TCO, captures the cost across the whole lifecycle of an investment, not just the purchase price.
Return on investment, or ROI, measures the relative return.
Net present value, or NPV, discounts future cash flows so that they can be compared fairly with money spent today.
The internal rate of return, or IRR, finds the discount rate at which an investment breaks even.
And payback measures how long it takes to recover the money invested.
Beyond individual calculations, portfolio evaluation balances strategic value against constraints.
When resources are limited, resource allocation addresses bottlenecks so that work can actually proceed.
Finally, governance and key performance indicators, or KPIs, ensure that investments deliver measurable benefits.
